scope: Open review section on hard-metal pneumoconiosis: cobalt-containing alloy exposure, hypersensitivity, ground-glass imaging, and giant-cell interstitial pneumonia.

keyRecommendations.text: Hard-metal pneumoconiosis is exposure to hard-metal alloy, largely tungsten and cobalt, not the generic term heavy metal.
It is a hypersensitivity reaction in susceptible workers. Imaging often shows diffuse ground-glass opacities, and biopsy is required.
The classic histology is giant-cell interstitial pneumonia.

clinicalBottomLine: Hard-metal lung disease is a hypersensitivity pneumoconiosis from tungsten-cobalt alloy dust. Expect ground-glass change, confirm with biopsy, and look for giant-cell interstitial pneumonia.
notableCaveats: An atypical letter without giant-cell interstitial pneumonia was not used. This is the hard-metal section of an open pneumoconiosis review.
